To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified and characterized the midgut transcriptomes of blood fed and sugar fed P. pernicious sand flies.

the midgut-specific transcriptome of Ph. perniciosis, a vector of visceral leichmaniasis in Europe, was characterized by sequencing two libraries and that the transcript expression profiles were compared between sugar-fed and blood-fed sand flies, and the results were discussed in light of previous findings in other sand flies.

we sequenced two cDNA libraries from the midgut tissue of the Old World vector P. perniciousus and compared their transcriptomes to identify molecules involved in blood digestion and immunity, and that we identified trypsin transcripts up regulated by L. infantum in this sand fly species.
In summary, our research is concerned with

identifying the molecular mechanisms of blood digestion and the interactions between L. infantum and its vector, which will contribute to a better understanding of the sand fly-parasite interaction and the transmission of visceral leishmaniases.
the identification of molecules involved in blood digestion and the interaction between L. infantum and its vector P. perniciousus.
the molecular basis for the interaction between sand flies and Leishmania parasites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work contributes to a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the digestion process in sand flies.
the midgut transcriptomic analysis of P. pernicousis provides insight into the molecular mechanisms involved in blood digestion and parasite development in the vector midgut.

the transcriptome analysis of P. perniciouss midgut provides new insights into molecules involved in blood digestion and immunity, and that the comparison of sugar fed versus blood fed libraries provides a better understanding of the midgut transcriptomic response to blood feeding in sand flies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study provides a valuable resource for future research on sand fly biology and the interaction with Leishmania parasites.
the midgut transcriptomes of sugar fed and fed sand flies were analyzed and the expression profiles of putative trypins were evaluated.

the midgut transcriptomic profile provides new insight on the digestive and immune processes of the midgut, and that the comparative analysis of these libraries will be useful for further studies on the molecular interactions between Leishmania parasites and sand flies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the P. perniosisus midgut transcript profile is similar to that of Phlebotonus papatasi, and different from Phlebotomous duboscqi and Lutzomyia longipalpis.
we have identified molecules with putative functions in blood meal digestion and immunity that can be further evaluated for their potential role in the vectorial competence of sand flies.

the P. perniosus midgut-specific transcriptome provides a rich source of information on the molecules expressed in this tissue and that the comparative analysis between sugar fed and blood-fed sand fly libraries provides a valuable resource for understanding the molecular basis of blood digestion in sand flies.
